To find the maximum number of black cubes, we can represent each unit cube by its coordinates \((x, y, z)\), where \(x, y, z \in \{1, 2, \dots, 2N+1\}\). 

Any \(2 \times 2 \times 2\) cube consists of unit cubes whose coordinates lie in \(\{x, x+1\} \times \{y, y+1\} \times \{z, z+1\}\) for some \(x, y, z \in \{1, 2, \dots, 2N\}\). Since any two consecutive integers contain exactly one even and one odd integer, each \(2 \times 2 \times 2\) cube contains exactly one unit cube of each of the 8 parity types \((x \bmod 2, y \bmod 2, z \bmod 2) \in \{0, 1\}^3\).

In the entire \((2N+1) \times (2N+1) \times (2N+1)\) cube, there are \(N+1\) odd coordinates and \(N\) even coordinates along each dimension. The number of unit cubes corresponding to each parity type depends on the number \(k \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}\) of odd coordinates:
- \(k = 3\) (all three coordinates odd): \((N+1)^3\) cubes (1 parity class)
- \(k = 2\) (two odd, one even): \((N+1)^2 N\) cubes (3 parity classes)
- \(k = 1\) (one odd, two even): \((N+1) N^2\) cubes (3 parity classes)
- \(k = 0\) (all three coordinates even): \(N^3\) cubes (1 parity class)

Since each \(2 \times 2 \times 2\) cube contains exactly one cube from each of the 8 parity classes, coloring any 4 of these parity classes black guarantees that every \(2 \times 2 \times 2\) cube contains exactly 4 black cubes, satisfying the condition.

To maximize the total number of black cubes, we select the 4 largest parity classes, which are the ones with \(k = 3\) and \(k = 2\):
\[
\text{Maximum black cubes} = (N+1)^3 + 3(N+1)^2 N = (N+1)^2 \big((N+1) + 3N\big) = (N+1)^2 (4N+1)
\]
Expanding this expression gives:
\[
4N^3 + 9N^2 + 6N + 1
\]

ANSWER: (N+1)^2(4N+1)
